description: Set up and maintain a healthy email list from collection through hygiene and segmentation.

steps.description: Design and deploy email collection points across owned channels.

inputs.name: business-context
inputs.desc: The business and what it offers

inputs.name: target-audience
inputs.desc: Who should be on the list

outputs.name: collection-points
outputs.desc: List of configured collection points (website forms, landing pages, checkout, in-app)

outputs.name: opt-in-flow
outputs.desc: The double opt-in confirmation flow

process: Identify every touchpoint where a visitor can subscribe (website header, footer, pop-up, checkout, blog sidebar, in-app).
Design each form with the minimum required fields (email, first name) plus any segmentation fields.
Set up the double opt-in confirmation email and landing page.
Configure the welcome email triggered on confirmation.

steps.description: Define and build segments for targeted sending.

outputs.name: segment-definitions
outputs.desc: Named segments with rules (demographics, behavior, engagement level, purchase history)

outputs.name: segment-map
outputs.desc: Map of which segments receive which content types

process: Define segments by demographics (location, role, industry) collected at sign-up.
Define segments by behavior (opened last 30 days, clicked last 7 days, purchased, abandoned cart).
Define engagement tiers (active, at-risk, dormant, churned) based on open and click recency.
Map each segment to the content types and frequency it should receive.

steps.description: Set up the list hygiene routine to keep deliverability high.

inputs.name: segment-definitions
inputs.desc: The segmentation rules including engagement tiers

outputs.name: hygiene-schedule
outputs.desc: Schedule for list cleaning tasks (bounce removal, re-engagement, sunset policy)

outputs.name: sunset-policy
outputs.desc: Rules for when to stop emailing and remove unengaged subscribers

process: Set the hard bounce removal rule (remove after first hard bounce).
Set the soft bounce escalation (remove after 3 consecutive soft bounces).
Design the re-engagement campaign for dormant subscribers (60 to 90 days inactive).
Define the sunset policy (remove after 120 days of zero engagement post re-engagement attempt).

steps.description: Plan and measure list growth tactics.

outputs.name: growth-tactics
outputs.desc: Ranked list of growth tactics with expected yield (lead magnets, referrals, partnerships, content upgrades)

outputs.name: list-management-plan
outputs.desc: The complete list management plan covering collection, segmentation, hygiene, and growth

process: Evaluate current growth rate and identify the gap to goal.
Design lead magnets for each major segment (ebook, checklist, template, free tool, webinar).
Plan referral and partnership tactics to reach new audiences.
Compile the full list management plan with metrics and review cadence.

description: Audit and optimize email deliverability from authentication through inbox placement.

steps.description: Audit DNS authentication records (SPF, DKIM, DMARC).

inputs.name: sending-domain
inputs.desc: The domain used for sending emails

inputs.name: email-service-provider
inputs.desc: The ESP or sending infrastructure in use

outputs.name: auth-audit-results
outputs.desc: Current state of SPF, DKIM, and DMARC records with pass/fail status

outputs.name: auth-fix-list
outputs.desc: List of DNS changes needed to fix authentication issues

process: Query the SPF record and verify it includes the ESP's sending IPs. Check for the 10-lookup limit.
Query the DKIM record and verify the public key matches the ESP configuration.
Query the DMARC record and verify the policy (none, quarantine, reject) and reporting addresses.
List every fix needed with the exact DNS record to add or change.

steps.description: Check the sender reputation across blacklists and reputation services.

outputs.name: reputation-scores
outputs.desc: Reputation scores from major services (Google Postmaster Tools, Microsoft SNDS, Sender Score)

outputs.name: blacklist-status
outputs.desc: Blacklist check results across major blacklists

process: Check the domain and sending IPs against major blacklists (Spamhaus, Barracuda, SORBS, SpamCop).
Pull reputation data from Google Postmaster Tools if available.
Check Microsoft SNDS for IP reputation.
Compile scores and flag any blacklist entries requiring delisting requests.

steps.description: Test inbox placement rates across major providers.

outputs.name: placement-results
outputs.desc: Inbox vs. spam vs. missing placement rates for Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo, and others

outputs.name: content-flags
outputs.desc: Content elements that triggered spam filters in testing

process: Send test emails to seed accounts across Gmail, Outlook, Yahoo, and Apple Mail.
Check where each test email landed (inbox, promotions tab, spam, not delivered).
Identify content patterns that correlate with spam placement (trigger words, link density, image-to-text ratio).
Record the placement rates and content flags.

steps.description: Produce the deliverability improvement plan with prioritized fixes.

outputs.name: improvement-plan
outputs.desc: Prioritized action plan for improving deliverability

outputs.name: monitoring-setup
outputs.desc: Ongoing monitoring configuration for deliverability metrics

process: Prioritize fixes by impact: authentication first, then blacklist delisting, then content fixes.
For each fix, document the exact change, who owns it, and the expected impact.
Set up ongoing monitoring (bounce rates, complaint rates, placement rates, authentication pass rates).
Define the alert thresholds that trigger investigation.

description: Run a newsletter from topic selection through send and performance review.

steps.description: Select and plan the newsletter topic and content structure.

inputs.name: audience-profile
inputs.desc: Who reads this newsletter and what they care about

inputs.name: content-calendar
inputs.desc: The editorial calendar for timing context

inputs.name: past-performance
inputs.desc: Performance data from recent issues (opens, clicks, replies)

outputs.name: issue-plan
outputs.desc: The plan for this issue: topic, sections, key links, and call to action

outputs.name: subject-line-candidates
outputs.desc: 3 to 5 subject line options to test

process: Review what performed well in recent issues (highest opens, highest clicks, most replies).
Identify the topic for this issue based on audience interest, timeliness, and editorial calendar.
Outline the sections (lead story, supporting content, links, CTA).
Write 3 to 5 subject line candidates for testing.

steps.description: Write the newsletter content from the issue plan.

inputs.name: issue-plan
inputs.desc: The issue plan with topic and sections

outputs.name: newsletter-draft
outputs.desc: The written newsletter content ready for design

outputs.name: preview-text
outputs.desc: The email preview text (first 90 characters visible in inbox)

process: Write the lead section: hook the reader in the first two sentences.
Write each supporting section with clear value and a link or takeaway.
Write the call to action (reply, click, share, buy).
Write the preview text that complements the subject line.

steps.description: Assemble the newsletter in the email template and prepare for send.

outputs.name: assembled-email
outputs.desc: The newsletter assembled in the email template, tested across clients

outputs.name: send-configuration
outputs.desc: Send settings (segment, send time, A/B test setup for subject lines)

process: Place the content into the newsletter template.
Add images, formatting, and links. Verify all links work.
Test rendering across email clients (Gmail, Outlook, Apple Mail, mobile).
Configure the send: select the segment, set the send time, configure subject line A/B test.

steps.description: Review the issue's performance and update the learnings.

outputs.name: issue-performance
outputs.desc: Performance metrics: open rate, click rate, unsubscribe rate, reply count, revenue if applicable

outputs.name: learnings-log
outputs.desc: What worked, what did not, and what to test next time

process: Pull performance data 48 hours after send (open rate, unique clicks, click-through rate, unsubscribes, bounces).
Compare against the rolling average for this newsletter.
Identify the winning subject line from the A/B test.
Log the learnings: what topic, format, or CTA performed above or below average.

description: Design and automate the subscriber lifecycle from welcome through re-engagement.

steps.description: Define the stages of the subscriber lifecycle and the triggers between them.

inputs.name: business-model
inputs.desc: How the business makes money (product sales, SaaS, services, content)

inputs.name: subscriber-data
inputs.desc: Available data points on subscribers (sign-up source, behavior, purchase history)

outputs.name: lifecycle-stages
outputs.desc: Named stages (new, engaged, customer, at-risk, dormant, churned) with entry and exit criteria

outputs.name: stage-triggers
outputs.desc: Events that move a subscriber from one stage to the next

process: Define each lifecycle stage based on engagement and purchase behavior.
Set the entry criteria for each stage (e.g., 'at-risk' = no open in 30 days).
Set the exit criteria (what moves them to the next stage or back to a prior one).
Map the triggers: which event fires which automation.

steps.description: Build the welcome email sequence for new subscribers.

inputs.name: business-model
inputs.desc: The business model for CTA context

outputs.name: welcome-sequence
outputs.desc: The sequence of welcome emails (timing, content, CTA for each)

outputs.name: welcome-metrics
outputs.desc: Target metrics for the welcome sequence (open rate, click rate, conversion rate)

process: Design email 1: immediate confirmation and brand introduction.
Design email 2 (day 1 to 2): deliver the promised value (lead magnet, first tip, onboarding).
Design email 3 (day 3 to 5): social proof and next step.
Design email 4 (day 7): the first ask (purchase, trial, deeper engagement).
Set target metrics for each email in the sequence.

steps.description: Build the re-engagement campaign for at-risk and dormant subscribers.

inputs.name: lifecycle-stages
inputs.desc: Stage definitions including at-risk and dormant criteria

inputs.name: stage-triggers
inputs.desc: The triggers that identify at-risk subscribers

outputs.name: re-engagement-sequence
outputs.desc: The re-engagement email sequence with timing and escalation

outputs.name: sunset-criteria
outputs.desc: When to stop attempting re-engagement and remove the subscriber

process: Design the re-engagement trigger (e.g., no open in 60 days).
Design email 1: 'We miss you' with a reason to come back (new content, offer, update).
Design email 2 (7 days later): direct ask -- 'Do you still want to hear from us?'
Design the sunset action: if no engagement after the sequence, suppress or remove.

steps.description: Document the full lifecycle automation and produce the implementation plan.

outputs.name: automation-map
outputs.desc: Visual map of all automations, triggers, and email sequences

outputs.name: lifecycle-plan
outputs.desc: The complete lifecycle management plan with implementation steps and success metrics

process: Map every automation: trigger event, email sequence, branching logic, exit conditions.
Document the data requirements for each trigger (what fields, what tracking).
Set the success metrics for each automation (conversion rate, engagement lift, churn reduction).
Compile the implementation plan with build order, testing, and launch timeline.

description: Build a reusable email template design system from brand standards through component library.

steps.description: Define the brand standards for email design.

inputs.name: brand-guidelines
inputs.desc: The brand's visual identity guidelines (colors, fonts, logo)

inputs.name: email-types
inputs.desc: Types of emails to design for (newsletter, transactional, promotional, lifecycle)

outputs.name: email-brand-spec
outputs.desc: Email-specific brand standards (colors as hex, web-safe font stack, logo sizing, spacing rules)

outputs.name: accessibility-rules
outputs.desc: Accessibility requirements (contrast ratios, alt text rules, font sizes, link styling)

process: Translate the brand colors to hex values and define background, text, link, button, and accent colors.
Select the web-safe font stack (primary + fallback) since custom fonts render inconsistently in email.
Set the logo placement, size, and alt text for email headers.
Define the accessibility rules: minimum 14px body text, 4.5:1 contrast ratio, alt text on every image.

steps.description: Build the reusable email components (header, footer, CTA buttons, content blocks).

outputs.name: component-library
outputs.desc: Library of reusable email components (header, footer, hero, text block, image block, CTA button, divider, social links)

outputs.name: component-usage-guide
outputs.desc: Guide showing when and how to use each component

process: Build the header component (logo, navigation links if any).
Build the footer component (unsubscribe link, address, social links, legal text).
Build content components: text block, image-left/image-right, hero image, CTA button, divider.
Test each component across email clients (Gmail, Outlook, Apple Mail, mobile) for rendering.

steps.description: Assemble the master templates from components for each email type.

outputs.name: master-templates
outputs.desc: One master template per email type, assembled from components and tested

outputs.name: template-design-system
outputs.desc: The complete design system document with components, templates, and usage rules

process: Assemble the newsletter template: header, hero, 2 to 3 content blocks, CTA, footer.
Assemble the transactional template: header, single content block, CTA, footer.
Assemble the promotional template: header, hero, offer block, CTA, footer.
Run the full rendering test suite across clients and compile the design system document.

description: Set up a structured A/B testing framework for email campaigns.

steps.description: Write the test hypothesis and define what to test.

inputs.name: campaign-context
inputs.desc: The email campaign or sequence being optimized

inputs.name: current-metrics
inputs.desc: Current performance metrics (open rate, click rate, conversion rate)

outputs.name: test-hypothesis
outputs.desc: The hypothesis: what change, what metric, what expected outcome

outputs.name: test-variables
outputs.desc: The specific variables to test (subject line, send time, CTA text, layout, personalization)

process: Identify the metric to improve (open rate = test subject/send time; click rate = test CTA/layout; conversion = test offer/landing page).
Write the hypothesis: 'Changing [variable] from [A] to [B] will increase [metric] by [X]% because [reason].'
Define the control (A) and variant (B). Change only one variable per test.
Set the success threshold (minimum lift to declare a winner).

steps.description: Design the test setup: sample size, duration, and split.

inputs.name: current-metrics
inputs.desc: Baseline metrics for sample size calculation

outputs.name: test-design
outputs.desc: Test configuration: sample size per variant, split percentage, send timing, and duration

outputs.name: statistical-plan
outputs.desc: The statistical method (significance level, minimum detectable effect, power)

process: Calculate the required sample size based on the baseline metric, minimum detectable effect, and 95% confidence.
Set the split (typically 50/50 for two variants, or 10/10/80 for subject line tests with auto-send winner to remainder).
Set the test duration (enough time to collect the required sample).
Document the statistical method and how the winner will be declared.

steps.description: Analyze the test results and determine the winner.

outputs.name: test-results
outputs.desc: Results per variant (metric values, confidence interval, statistical significance)

outputs.name: test-conclusion
outputs.desc: Winner declaration, whether the hypothesis was confirmed, and the recommended next test

process: Pull the results for each variant after the test duration.
Calculate the statistical significance (p-value or confidence interval).
Declare the winner if significance is reached; declare inconclusive if not.
Document the learning and recommend the next test to run.

description: Set up transactional email infrastructure from identification through monitoring.

steps.description: Inventory all transactional emails the system needs to send.

inputs.name: application-context
inputs.desc: The application or service that sends transactional emails

inputs.name: user-journey-map
inputs.desc: The user journey showing where emails are triggered

outputs.name: email-inventory
outputs.desc: List of every transactional email: trigger event, recipient, content purpose, priority

outputs.name: delivery-requirements
outputs.desc: Delivery requirements per email (latency SLA, retry policy, fallback)

process: Walk through the user journey and list every event that triggers an email (sign-up, password reset, order confirmation, shipping update, payment receipt, etc.).
For each email, note the trigger event, who receives it, what information it must contain, and the urgency.
Set the delivery SLA for each (e.g., password reset under 30 seconds, order confirmation under 2 minutes).
Define the retry policy for failed sends.

steps.description: Build the templates for each transactional email.

outputs.name: transactional-templates
outputs.desc: Templates for each email with dynamic variable placeholders

outputs.name: template-test-results
outputs.desc: Rendering test results across email clients

process: Design the base transactional template (clean, minimal, fast-loading).
Build each email template with the required dynamic variables (user name, order ID, amount, link, etc.).
Test rendering across email clients.
Verify that all dynamic variables render correctly with sample data.

steps.description: Configure the sending infrastructure and API integration.

outputs.name: send-configuration
outputs.desc: API integration configuration (provider, API keys, endpoint, headers, payload format)

outputs.name: retry-configuration
outputs.desc: Retry and fallback configuration for failed sends

process: Select and configure the transactional email provider (or self-hosted SMTP).
Set up the API integration: authentication, endpoint, payload format for each template.
Configure the retry logic (exponential backoff, max retries, fallback provider if available).
Set up the webhook for delivery status callbacks (delivered, bounced, complained).

steps.description: Set up monitoring and alerting for transactional email delivery.

outputs.name: monitoring-dashboard
outputs.desc: Dashboard configuration for send volume, delivery rate, bounce rate, latency

outputs.name: transactional-email-plan
outputs.desc: The complete transactional email plan covering inventory, templates, infrastructure, and monitoring

process: Configure the monitoring dashboard: send volume, delivery rate, bounce rate, complaint rate, average latency.
Set alerts for SLA breaches (latency over threshold, delivery rate drop, bounce spike).
Set up the log pipeline for debugging individual send failures.
Compile the full transactional email plan.

description: Set up email compliance for CAN-SPAM, GDPR, and CASL from audit through documentation.

steps.description: Audit current email practices against applicable regulations.

inputs.name: sending-regions
inputs.desc: Where recipients are located (US, EU, Canada, other)

inputs.name: current-practices
inputs.desc: Current email collection, sending, and unsubscribe practices

outputs.name: regulation-applicability
outputs.desc: Which regulations apply (CAN-SPAM, GDPR, CASL, ePrivacy) and why

outputs.name: compliance-gaps
outputs.desc: List of gaps between current practices and regulatory requirements

process: Determine which regulations apply based on sender location, recipient location, and business type.
Audit current consent collection against each regulation's requirements (opt-in vs. opt-out, explicit vs. implied).
Audit the unsubscribe mechanism (timing, ease, confirmation).
Audit data storage and retention practices against GDPR requirements.

steps.description: Design the consent collection and management system.

outputs.name: consent-framework
outputs.desc: Consent collection requirements per regulation (opt-in type, proof of consent, retention period)

outputs.name: consent-ux-specs
outputs.desc: UX specifications for consent collection (form language, checkbox behavior, confirmation flow)

process: For each applicable regulation, document the consent standard required (express consent, implied consent, opt-out).
Design the consent collection UX: unchecked checkboxes for GDPR, clear language, granular preferences.
Design the consent record: what to store (timestamp, IP, form version, exact language consented to).
Design the consent withdrawal (unsubscribe) flow meeting the strictest applicable standard.

steps.description: Build the unsubscribe mechanism to meet all regulatory requirements.

outputs.name: unsubscribe-spec
outputs.desc: The unsubscribe mechanism specification (one-click, preference center, confirmation page)

outputs.name: processing-timeline
outputs.desc: The unsubscribe processing timeline and verification procedure

process: Implement the one-click unsubscribe header (RFC 8058, required by Gmail and Yahoo since 2024).
Design the preference center (unsubscribe from specific types vs. all).
Set the processing timeline (CAN-SPAM allows 10 business days; best practice is immediate).
Test the full unsubscribe flow from link click through suppression.

steps.description: Produce the compliance documentation and ongoing audit schedule.

inputs.name: compliance-gaps
inputs.desc: The original gaps for tracking fixes

outputs.name: compliance-documentation
outputs.desc: The complete compliance documentation (policies, procedures, consent records, unsubscribe process)

outputs.name: audit-schedule
outputs.desc: Schedule for periodic compliance audits (quarterly review, annual full audit)

process: Document the privacy policy sections covering email collection and use.
Document the consent record-keeping procedure and retention period.
Document the unsubscribe process with the processing timeline commitment.
Set the audit schedule: quarterly spot check, annual full audit, triggered audit on regulation changes.

description: Migrate email infrastructure from one provider to another without losing data or deliverability.

steps.description: Audit the current state and plan what needs to migrate.

inputs.name: migration-reason
inputs.desc: Why the migration is happening (cost, features, deliverability, consolidation)

outputs.name: migration-inventory
outputs.desc: Everything that needs to migrate: lists, segments, templates, automations, integrations, historical data

outputs.name: risk-assessment
outputs.desc: Risks to deliverability, data integrity, and business continuity during migration

process: Inventory the source provider: subscriber lists, segments, custom fields, tags.
Inventory templates, automations (flows/sequences), and active campaigns.
Inventory integrations (CRM, ecommerce, analytics, API connections).
Assess risks: deliverability impact of IP/domain warm-up, data loss, downtime, broken automations.

steps.description: Plan the migration sequence and timeline.

outputs.name: migration-plan
outputs.desc: Step-by-step migration plan with sequence, timeline, and rollback checkpoints

outputs.name: warmup-plan
outputs.desc: IP and domain warm-up plan for the new provider

process: Plan the migration sequence: DNS first, then lists, then templates, then automations, then active campaigns.
Design the IP warm-up schedule (start with most engaged segment, gradually increase volume over 2 to 4 weeks).
Set rollback checkpoints at each phase (if deliverability drops below X%, pause and investigate).
Schedule the cutover window with a parallel sending period for validation.

steps.description: Execute the migration and validate each phase.

outputs.name: migration-log
outputs.desc: Log of each migration step with status, issues encountered, and resolutions

outputs.name: validation-results
outputs.desc: Validation results for each migrated component (list counts match, templates render, automations fire)

process: Execute DNS changes (SPF, DKIM for new provider). Verify authentication passes.
Export and import subscriber lists. Verify counts match and custom fields mapped correctly.
Recreate templates in the new provider. Test rendering.
Recreate automations and test each trigger fires correctly.

steps.description: Complete the migration, decommission the old provider, and document the new state.

outputs.name: cutover-confirmation
outputs.desc: Confirmation that all sending is on the new provider with no remaining dependencies on the old

outputs.name: migration-report
outputs.desc: The complete migration report: what moved, what changed, lessons learned, new provider documentation

process: Confirm all active campaigns and automations are running on the new provider.
Verify no sends are going through the old provider.
Update all integrations to point to the new provider's API.
Decommission the old provider account (after a 30-day overlap for safety) and compile the migration report.

description: Build an email analytics dashboard from metric definition through automated reporting.

steps.description: Define the email KPIs and their calculation methods.

inputs.name: email-program-scope
inputs.desc: The scope of the email program (newsletter, lifecycle, transactional, promotional)

inputs.name: business-goals
inputs.desc: What the email program should achieve for the business

outputs.name: kpi-definitions
outputs.desc: Defined KPIs with formulas, data sources, and benchmarks (open rate, click rate, conversion rate, revenue per email, list growth rate, churn rate)

outputs.name: reporting-dimensions
outputs.desc: The dimensions to slice data by (campaign type, segment, time period, device, email client)

process: Define each KPI: name, formula, data source, industry benchmark, internal target.
Include health metrics (bounce rate, complaint rate, unsubscribe rate) alongside performance metrics.
Define the dimensions for slicing: by campaign type, by segment, by time (daily, weekly, monthly), by device.
Set the data refresh frequency for each metric.

steps.description: Build the data pipeline from the ESP to the analytics layer.

outputs.name: data-pipeline
outputs.desc: The data pipeline configuration (source APIs, transformations, storage, refresh schedule)

outputs.name: data-model
outputs.desc: The data model for the analytics layer (tables, relationships, calculated fields)

process: Configure the data extract from the ESP API (send events, open events, click events, bounce events, unsubscribe events).
Transform the raw events into the metrics defined in the KPIs.
Build the data model with fact and dimension tables.
Set the refresh schedule and monitor for data freshness.

steps.description: Design the dashboard layout and visualizations.

inputs.name: data-model
inputs.desc: The data model powering the dashboard

outputs.name: dashboard-layout
outputs.desc: The dashboard layout with sections (overview, campaign detail, segment comparison, health metrics)

outputs.name: visualization-specs
outputs.desc: Specifications for each chart (type, metric, dimensions, filters)

process: Design the overview section: headline metrics with period-over-period trend arrows.
Design the campaign detail section: table of recent campaigns with sortable performance columns.
Design the segment comparison section: side-by-side performance by segment.
Design the health section: bounce rate, complaint rate, and list growth trend lines.

steps.description: Set up automated reporting from the dashboard.

outputs.name: automated-reports
outputs.desc: Configuration for automated report delivery (weekly digest, monthly review, alert-triggered)

outputs.name: email-analytics-plan
outputs.desc: The complete email analytics plan covering KPIs, pipeline, dashboard, and reporting

process: Configure the weekly digest email with headline metrics and top/bottom campaigns.
Configure the monthly review report with trend analysis and segment insights.
Configure alert-triggered reports for anomalies (bounce spike, complaint rate over 0.1%, significant drop in open rate).
Compile the full email analytics plan.
